topics.label: Introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture by connecting it to the practicals and outlining its learning outcomes.

topics.label: Tumor virology and the discovery of cellular proto-oncogenes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how investigations of cancer-causing viruses revealed that transformation originates in altered cellular genes.

topics.label: Experimental tests of cellular transformation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how experimental assays establish whether a gene or mutation gives cells transformed properties.

topics.label: Cancer gene classification and the functional effects of mutations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cancer mutations are classified by their functional effects, using cell-cycle regulation and mutation dominance to illustrate and qualify those classifications.

topics.label: Genetic instability and its role in tumor progression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how failures of genome maintenance generate genetic instability that changes the course of tumor development.

topics.label: Hereditary cancer predisposition and the consequences of tumor-suppressor mutations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics follow inherited tumor-suppressor defects through cancer development, with BRCA2 restoration illustrating why the initiating defect need not remain necessary for malignancy.

topics.label: Closing, further reading, and questions
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture with an invitation for questions, recommended reading, and a preview of the next lecture.
